items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we'll learn to compare numbers expressed in scientific notation.

Content:
For example, suppose we want to compare the following two numbers:

Content:
[MATH: 7.4 \times 10^{5}, \qquad 6.5 \times 10^{5}]

Content:
To determine which of them is larger, we note the following:

Content:
- Our numbers contain the same power of ten [MATH: \left(10^{\color{blue}5}\right).]
- When the powers of ten are the same, we only need to compare the decimal parts.

Content:
Now, since [MATH: {\color{red}7.4}] is larger than [MATH: {\color{red}6.5},] i.e.,

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}7.4} \:\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{> }\: {\color{red}6.5}]

Content:
we can write down the following comparison statement:

Content:
[MATH: \left({\color{red}7.4} \times 10^{\color{blue}5}\right) \:\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{> }\: \left( {\color{red}6.5} \times 10^{\color{blue}5} \right)]

  3. [MATH: <]

Notice that our numbers contain the same power of ten, namely, [MATH: 10^{\color{blue}-4}.]

To compare numbers in scientific notation with the same power of ten, we compare their decimal parts.

Since [MATH: {\color{red}7.1} < {\color{red}8.45},] we have

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this lesson, we'll learn to compare numbers expressed in scientific notation.

Content:
For example, suppose we want to compare the following two numbers:

Content:
[MATH: 7.4 \times 10^{5}, \qquad 6.5 \times 10^{5}]

Content:
To determine which of them is larger, we note the following:

Content:
- Our numbers contain the same power of ten [MATH: \left(10^{\color{blue}5}\right).]
- When the powers of ten are the same, we only need to compare the decimal parts.

Content:
Now, since [MATH: {\color{red}7.4}] is larger than [MATH: {\color{red}6.5},] i.e.,

Content:
[MATH: {\color{red}7.4} \:\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{> }\: {\color{red}6.5}]

Content:
we can write down the following comparison statement:

Content:
[MATH: \left({\color{red}7.4} \times 10^{\color{blue}5}\right) \:\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{> }\: \left( {\color{red}6.5} \times 10^{\color{blue}5} \right)]

---

Item 2 — Example: Comparing Numbers in Scientific Notation: Same Powers of Ten

Which symbols could replace the empty box above to make the statement true?

1. [MATH: >]
2. [MATH: =]
3. [MATH: <]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Notice that our numbers contain the same power of ten, namely, [MATH: 10^{\color{blue}-4}.]

To compare numbers in scientific notation with the same power of ten, we compare their decimal parts.

Since [MATH: {\color{red}7.1} < {\color{red}8.45},] we have

[MATH: \left({\color{red}7.1} \times 10^{\color{blue}-4}\right) \:\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{ < }\: \left( {\color{red}8.45} \times 10^{\color{blue}-4} \right).]

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

Item 9 — Example: Comparing Numbers in Scientific Notation: Different Powers of Ten, Negative Exponents

Example Prompt:
[MATH: \left(7.1 \times 10^{-3}\right) \:\bbox[3pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\: \left( 8.7 \times 10^{-4} \right)]

1. [MATH: >]
2. [MATH: =]
3. [MATH: <]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Notice that our numbers contain different powers of ten:

- [MATH: 7.1 \times 10^{\color{blue}-3}] contains the [MATH: {\color{blue}-3}]rd power of ten
- [MATH: 8.7 \times 10^{\color{blue}-4}] contains the [MATH: {\color{blue}-4}]th power of ten

Since [MATH: {\color{blue}-3} > {\color{blue}-4},] we have

[MATH: \left( 7.1 \times 10^{\color{blue}-3}\right) \:\bbox[3pt, Gainsboro]{ > }\: \left( 8.7 \times 10^{\color{blue}-4} \right).]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
